newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli legislators visit PLO Jerusalem office.
newsitem.headline: Israeli legislators visit PLO Jerusalem office.

text.p: A handful of members of an Israeli parliamentary committee visited Orient House, the PLO's Jerusalem headquarters, on Sunday in defiance of government policy.

The visit, boycotted by most of the members of the Knesset's Interior Committee, coincided with Israeli diplomatic efforts to persuade the fact-finding "troika" of the European Union foreign ministers not to hold talks with Palestinians at Orient House.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Saturday it was vital the troika visit Israel in the near future and also hold talks with the PLO.
Committee chairman Salah Tarif of the main opposition Labour party organised the visit, hosted by Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem.
He was accompanied by committee members Micha Goldman and Rafi Elul, both also Labour legislators. Right-wing and religious members of the 15-member committee stayed away.
"We came to visit Orient House as a parliamentary committee to speak about the affairs of the residents of East Jerusalem," Tarif told reporters.

The building, in Arab East Jerusalem, is a symbol of the PLO's nationalist aspirations and its desire to make the eastern part of the city, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, capital of a future Palestinian state.
Israel regards all of Jerusalem as its capital, a claim that has failed to win international recognition.
Israeli leaders have warned the PLO not to conduct at Orient House any activity associated with Palestinian self-rule, in effect only in parts of the West Bank and Gaza.
